boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.

boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro: Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow. 8 players competed in a chess tournament, marked with the letters A-H. The tournament had three stages, each of which is represented in the graph by a circle. The sequence of games of each player in the tournament is presented by means of squares that are connected by arrows. The filling of each square indicates the duration of the game (see key). The first game of each player is represented by the square adjacent to the player's letter. From this square an arrow comes out that points to the next game, and so on. If a game in the tournament ended in a draw, the two players played another game against each other at the same stage. If a game ended in a decision, the winner advanced to the next stage in the tournament, and the loser left the tournament. For example, in the first stage of the tournament player G played one game, and this game lasted more than three hours. It can be deduced that at this stage he played against player D, since player D is the only one who also played only one game in the first stage that lasted more than 3 hours.

Study the table below, then answer the five questions that follow. The table presents data that were recorded at the end of the year 2020, on the fruits that are infested with pests in a certain orchard of plum trees. The plum trees in the orchard are planted in 7 plots, which are marked in the table with the letters A to G. Inside the plots the trees are planted in rows. The number of rows in each plot is indicated in the table beneath the name of the plot. In each row in the orchard 4 trees are planted, one tree from each of four plum varieties: A, B, C and D. For each variety of plums, the percentage of the fruits that are infested with pests in each plot is written in the table. The plum trees in each of the plots were planted at the end of the year of planting indicated at the bottom of the table. Note: In all the questions assume that each one of the trees in the orchard has an equal number of plums. For example: The trees in plot D were planted at the end of the year 2005. In this plot there are 4 rows of trees (in each row 4 plum trees, one from each variety, and altogether there are 16 plum trees in the plot). 25% of the plums of variety B in this plot are infested with pests.

questions.stem:
If y candies are divided equally among 2 children, one candy is left over.
If y candies are divided equally among 3 children, one candy is left over.
If y candies are divided equally among 4 children, one candy is left over.

y can be equal to –

methods.text: Remainder 1 on division by 2, 3 and 4 means \(y-1\) is divisible by all three — that is, by their LCM, 12. So \(y = 12k + 1\).
The candidates are 13, 25, 37, and only 13 is on the list. Note that checking all three conditions separately works too, but the LCM step turns three tests into one.

What is the volume of the fourth cube that Liat placed (in cm³)?

w, x, y and z are four positive numbers that are different from each other.

Given:  m is the average of w and x .
     5m is the average of y and z .

What is the average of w, x, y and z ?

methods.text: \(a^{2x} = \left(a^x\right)^2 = 8\), so \(a^x = \sqrt8 = 2\sqrt2\), taking the positive root since \(a>0\).
Square each option: \(2^2=4\), \(\left(2\sqrt2\right)^2 = 8\) ✓. Squaring four options is faster than manipulating the given.

questions.stem: x, y and z are integers that are different from zero: x and y are odd, and z is even. Which of the following numbers is necessarily not an integer?

methods.text: Track parity through each option. \(xy\) is odd times odd, so odd; \(xy + z\) is odd plus even, so odd. An odd number divided by an even number can never be an integer, because the numerator has no factor of 2 to give.
The others can all come out whole: \(\frac{x+z}y\) at \(x=1,z=2,y=3\) is 1 ✓; \(\frac{x+y+z}{z}\) at \(x=y=1,z=2\) is 2 ✓; \(\frac{zx}y\) at \(z=2,x=3,y=1\) is 6 ✓.

questions.stem: In a jar there are balls in different colours. 50% of the balls are green, and 25% of the balls are red. 20% of the balls that are not green are yellow. What percentage of the balls in the jar, at most, are blue?

methods.text: Green is 50%, so non-green is 50%. Yellow is 20% of that, which is 10% of the jar. With red at 25%, the accounted total is \(50+25+10 = 85\%\), leaving at most 15% blue.
The 20% is of the non-green balls, not of the jar. Applying it to the jar gives 5% and option (1).

questions.stem:
A and B are digits between 1 and 9.

Given: the two-digit number AB is 9 times as much as the sum of its digits.

How many values can the number AB have?

methods.text: \(\overline{AB} = 9(A+B)\) gives \(10A + B = 9A + 9B\), so \(A = 8B\). Only \(B = 1\) keeps \(A\) a digit, giving \(A = 8\) and the number 81.
One value. The relation \(A = 8B\) collapses immediately because \(B = 2\) would already need \(A = 16\).

questions.stem:
Dror works 100 hours a month, earns 10 dollars an hour, and pays taxes in the amount of 4% of his wages.
In a certain month Dror's wage rose to 20 dollars an hour, and likewise the percentage of taxes that he pays rose to 20%.

How many hours will Dror have to work from now on each month so that his wages, after the payment of taxes, will not change?

methods.text: Now: \(100 \times 10 \times 0.96 = 960\) after tax. Then: \(h \times 20 \times 0.8 = 16h\). Setting \(16h = 960\) gives \(h = 60\).
Both the wage and the tax rate changed, so the take-home per hour must be recomputed from scratch rather than scaled.

questions.stem: Eran stood on some stair on a staircase. Every minute he climbed 10 stairs or descended one stair. After A minutes Eran stood on a stair adjacent to the stair from which he began to walk on the stairs. Which of the following numbers can be equal to A?

methods.text: With \(u\) climbs and \(d\) descents, \(u + d = A\) and \(10u - d = \pm1\). Adding gives \(11u = A \pm 1\), so \(A\) must be one away from a multiple of 11.

Of 8, 9, 10 and 11, only \(A = 10\) satisfies it: \(u = 1\), \(d = 9\), net \(+1\).

A divisibility condition hidden inside a rate question.

How many girls, at most, are holding hands with two boys?
How many numbers between 10 and 12 (not including 10 and 12) have a product with 3 that is an integer?

methods.text: The question is asking which numbers strictly between 10 and 12 give a whole number when multiplied by 3 — that is, numbers whose thirds are whole.
Those are the numbers of the form \(\frac k3\) in that range: \(\frac{31}3, \frac{32}3, 11, \frac{34}3, \frac{35}3\) — five of them, since \(k\) runs from 31 to 35.
Over the common denominator 20: \(\frac{3}{20} + \frac{14}{20} + \frac{10}{20} - \frac{7}{20} = \frac{20}{20} = 1\). The multiplication is done first.

In the last 7 years the population of city A grew by 7,015 people on average per year, whereas the population of city B grew in this period by 6,985 people on average per year. 7 years ago the populations of the two cities were equal in size. By how many people is the population of city A larger than the population of city B today?

methods.text: Only the difference in growth matters: \(7015 - 6985 = 30\) people a year.
Over 7 years that is 210. The populations themselves are never needed and are not given.

questions.stem:
The accompanying figure shows that ABCDEF is a regular hexagon.
Given:  CE ⊥ DG

\(\dfrac{DG}{\text{the perimeter of the hexagon}} = ?\)

methods.text: Over the common denominator \((x-1)(x+1) = x^2-1\), the numerator is \((x+1)^2 + (x-1)^2 = 2x^2+2\), so the sum is \(\dfrac{2x^2+2}{x^2-1}\).
Take \(x=2\): the expression is \(3 + \frac13 = \frac{10}{3}\). Option (3) gives \(\frac{10}{3}\); the others give 1, \(-2\) and \(\frac53\).

questions.stem:
A television series is divided into a number of seasons, and in each season there are 13 episodes.

To which season does the 120th episode in the series belong?

methods.text: Each season holds 13 episodes, so episode 120 sits in season \(\lceil 120/13 \rceil\). Since \(13 \times 9 = 117\) and \(13 \times 10 = 130\), episode 120 is in season 10.
The rounding direction is the whole question: \(120 \div 13\) is about 9.2, and a fraction of a season still counts as that season, so round up, not down.

questions.stem: How many even divisors does the number 40 have (not including 40 itself)?

methods.text: \(40 = 2^3 \cdot 5\). Its even divisors are exactly the divisors that keep at least one factor of 2: \(2, 4, 8, 10, 20, 40\) — six of them.
Excluding 40 itself leaves five. A quicker route: even divisors of \(N\) are \(2 \times\) the divisors of \(N/2\), and \(20 = 2^2 \cdot 5\) has \(3 \times 2 = 6\) divisors.

questions.stem: Avi washes the staircase in 3 hours. Guy washes the staircase at a rate that is equal to that of Avi. One day Avi and Guy began to wash the staircase together. After an hour Avi continued on his own until he finished the washing. How many hours did Avi work on his own?

methods.text: Equal rates, so together they work at \(\frac23\) of a staircase an hour. One hour leaves \(\frac13\).
Avi alone does \(\frac13\) an hour, so exactly 1 more hour. Multi-phase accounting with the tidiest possible numbers.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(|x| \cdot (x - 2) \leq 0\)

The exact range in which x is found is –

methods.text: \(|x|\) is never negative, so it can never supply a minus. The product is at most 0 when \(x-2\le0\), that is \(x\le2\) — and also at \(x=0\), where \(|x|\) is 0, which is already inside that range.
One factor has a fixed sign and the other carries the whole question. Once you see that \(|x|\ge0\) always, the inequality reduces to \(x-2\le0\).
\(x=3\) gives \(3\cdot1>0\) ✗, and \(x=-3\) gives \(3\cdot(-5)<0\) ✓. So negatives are in and values above 2 are out — which only option (2) manages.

The price of bread, milk and cottage cheese is k shekels.
The price of bread and cottage cheese is m shekels.
The price of bread and milk is n shekels.

What is the price of the bread (in shekels)?

methods.text: Add the last two: \((B+C) + (B+M) = m+n\), which is \(B + (B+M+C) = B + k\). So \(B = m+n-k\).
Give the three items values — bread 3, milk 4, cheese 5 — so \(k=12\), \(m=8\), \(n=7\). Then \(m+n-k = 3\), the price of bread ✓. One set of values separates all four options.
